summary: NC.6 is a process endpoint whose outputs belong to NC.1–NC.5 and EffectiveDiophantineMethods ED.6. This continuation indexes the fine-grained supplier exports and their exact locus, path and height conventions, while retaining their hypotheses and open gaps. Coverage remains partial: no accepted restructuring result drops NC.6, and the checker rejects both node-free planned closure and an under-budget complete pass with an open scope.

sourceIssues.locator: Published Lemma 4.7, p.1136; same tail condition in arXiv:2101.01862v4, p.25.
sourceIssues.printed: The truncation index is constrained only at coefficient indices satisfying ord_p(F_i) + i = n.
sourceIssues.correction: For all i ≥ m require ord_p(F_i) + i ≥ n, using ord_p(0) = infinity; retain the convergence and multiplicity obligations of the ED.6 root-determination-precision node.
sourceIssues.reason: The coefficient of T^i in G(T) = p^(−k)F(pT) has valuation ord_p(F_i) + i − k. A polynomial truncation of degree below m modulo p^(n−k) therefore needs a bound for every tail index. For F(x) = p^5 − p x + x^2, m = 2, n = 5, k = 2, the only equality index is 0, whereas G(T) = p^3 − T + T^2 has a unit coefficient in degree 2. This repeats the obstruction already recorded by the ED supplier; it supplies no new root-isolation proof.
sourceIssues.known: Already recorded as EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E21, confirmed by REV-EffectiveDiophantineMethods~3. Freshly checked here in the published and v4 passages; not claimed new.

sourceIssues.locator: arXiv:2101.01862v4, p.24, final branch equality before Proposition 4.6; compared with published (4.21), p.1134, and branch equality, p.1136.

sourceIssues.correction: The branch is phi(i) = −2 floor(log_p i). Add c1 when applying the separate splitting estimate, as in the final coefficient bound.
sourceIssues.reason: Substituting the eventual minimum into the published definition (4.21) gives two negative floor-log terms. The published branch agrees; c1 remains in Proposition 4.6's final bound.

frontiers: Mochizuki's closed-curve Isom theorem is not the section conjecture and supplies no rational-point enumeration algorithm. Hom claims and variants for other bases require their own NC.1 sources.

A finite-level locus contains the specified global rational or integral points through the local/global diagram. Finiteness under verified dimension or quadratic-height hypotheses is distinct from equality with the global set.

Eventual equality in BDCKW §3.1 uses that source's minimal Z-model and stringent local conditions. Do not generalize it to arbitrary number fields or identify it with Kim 2009 Conjecture 1's dimension inequality.

Any unresolved Bloch–Kato, Fontaine–Mazur, logarithm-rank, reduction or local-height input remains an explicit condition on every downstream assertion. FAIL or unresolved candidate balls yield an open computation.

supplierExports.conditions: Use continuous arithmetic extension equivalences over the fixed G_K, modulo target geometric inner conjugation. Distinguish the pointed Theorem 10.1 from the outer-action Theorem 10.2; the unpointed extension formulation retains the NC.1 comparison obligations. The supplier is under revision, so this index does not certify its statement or close its four gaps.

supplierExports.output: Geometric unipotent groups, tensor paths and comparisons
supplierExports.conditions: Use functors on all coefficient algebras and geometric right path torsors, rather than pointwise topological H1. Retain the length transitions, composition, filtration and Frobenius. The ramified base-change clause covers models and endpoints descending from the stated unramified setup; general ramified-model comparison remains requested.

Retain every specified bad-place and crystalline local condition, actual localization natural transformations and their all-algebra representability hypotheses. The closed fibre-product construction does not supply its own representability inputs. The parent topological torsor-classification node is not a substitute.

supplierExports.output: Albanese coordinates, local loci and conditional finiteness
supplierExports.conditions: With the supplier right-path convention, the period representative is I(b,x) inverse times gamma(x). Preserve the distinct crystalline, de Rham period-image and geometric-image-closure loci and their forward inclusions. The selected dimension theorem over Q assumes a verified strict inequality and all geometric inputs; it proves finiteness, not eventual global-point equality.

supplierExports.output: Quadratic pairs, signed away-place heights and finite supersets
supplierExports.conditions: The rank criterion uses the rational Neron-Severi rank and the Mordell-Weil-cut Selmer convention. Upsilon is the negative sum of all away-place height alternatives. A finite residual locus is a superset of the rational points and need not equal the exact depth-two locus. Preserve analytic density on every open subdisc and compact chart coverage; certify the logarithm separately when ED.6 requires it.

supplierExports.output: Finite precision, exhaustive local root coverage and exact global certification
supplierExports.conditions: ED.6 owns finite coefficient/precision data, sound exhaustive root or disc coverage, simple-root uniqueness or its separately justified replacement, and matching or exclusion of every candidate against exact global points. Its review remains needs_changes. NC.6 supplies no root-isolation theorem, verifier or numerical replay and adds no reconstruction dependency to this algorithm.
